right.tested_scope: Mechanism-supporting evidence for editable persistent repair memory: SpaceMind converts episode outcomes into persistent skill mutations that can create, rewrite or disable strategies and gates proposed mutations for quality/safety before reuse. In the reported self-evolution study four of six groups recover after a single failed episode, including one complete-failure group reaching 100% success and an inspection score improving from 12 to 59; the same codebase reports 100% rendezvous success in its physical-robot validation. The source checkpoint explicitly limits the inference: this robotics evidence is only directionally consistent with revocable repair support and is not a matched autonomous-science ablation in which a false persistent scientific constraint is explicitly revoked and a previously excluded optimum is recovered.

overlap_dimensions: Both preserve state across a failure boundary and consult that state before a consequential later action: reconcile durable external-effect state before execute/recertify on the left, and apply persistent repair mutations plus a quality/safety gate before strategy reuse on the right.
Both are designed to prevent unsafe continuation after failure, but the protected object differs: external side-effect execution state versus reusable learned strategy state.
disjoint_dimensions: Execution substrate: deterministic crash-prone controller/provider recovery versus embodied-agent skill evolution and robotics validation.
Control mechanism: durable intent, stable effect identity and authoritative provider reconciliation versus create/rewrite/disable skill mutations plus a mutation quality/safety gate.

Measured outcome: exact execute/reconcile counts and certificate stability across six SIGKILL boundaries versus post-failure group recovery, inspection-score improvement and physical rendezvous success.
Failure mode: duplicate or inconsistent external effects after process death versus sticky or non-revocable bad repair memory that cannot be corrected before reuse.
Scope limit: constrained provider idempotency/reconciliation model versus robotics mechanism-support only, with no matched science-domain false-constraint revocation and recovered optimum.
comparison.material_difference: terminal_outer_sigkill_reference is executed process-death recovery evidence for suppressing duplicate external effects under a constrained provider contract. revocable_repair_support is cross-domain evidence that persistent repair memory can be edited or disabled after failure and gated before reuse. Their identities, interventions, metrics, protected state and failure modes are distinct, and neither tested scope subsumes the other.
